headline: Approved $10,000 donation to Art City and voted to oppose repeal of camper/RV ordinance 0-26-005.
summary: The committee voted to send a letter opposing the repeal of Ordinance 0-26-005, which bans campers and recreational vehicles downtown. It also approved a $10,000 donation to Art City for its August mural program and discussed past ICON architecture expenses and upcoming downtown events.
decisions: Voted unanimously to have chair Blaisdell send a letter opposing repeal of Ordinance 0-26-005.
Approved $10,000 donation to Art City for its August mural program, motion by Edward Hayes, seconded by Elisa Drift, unanimously approved.

plain_text:
Minutes 
Downtown Improvement Committee 
August 14, 2026 
Attending: Marylou Blaisdell, Fouad Mahfuz, Edward Haynes, Elisa Drift, Phillip Sconstas, 
Michael Buckley, Liz Hannan, Rich Lannan, Cole Morgan – via phone  
Also, in attendance Alyssa O’Mera – GAD, Alderman Amber Morgan 
Meeting started 7:45 a.m. room 208 City Hall 
Discussion Points 
1. Ordinance 0-26-005 Repealing the prohibition of Campers and recreational vehicles 
a. Committee discussed impact of the downtown.  The downtown business owners 
have seen a big improvement since camping has been prohibited. The downtown 
police officer has been excellent and very supportive. 
b. The committee unanimously voted for chair Blaisdell to send a letter to the Chief 
of Police stating we were opposed of any repealing of this ordinance. 
2. Financial – a report dated 2021- 2025 for expenditures accounted to our committee.  
Several expenses are in question – all from ICON architecture.  Discussion on how 
monies can be used and what expenses the committee voted to spend.  Liz stated the 
ICON expenses can be paid by TIF monies, and she and Alderwoman Morgan will 
review and bring information to the committee. 
a. Edward Hayes requested a complete report of all expenditures, Liz  will request 
the reports. 
3. Art City 
a. Art City has requested a $5,000 donation for their August mural program.  This 
program would include 4 large professional murals that will be painted along 
Nashua’s Heritage Rail Trail, and 10 8x10 murals will be live painted along the 
trail behind 809 Lounge and they will revamp the Land China building, they will 
also include programs for kids and families. 
b. Liz stated the group is very involved in the community, and their fundraising 
efforts have been very good, they have a 10,000 deficient.  After discussion a 
motion was made by Edward Hayes to approve 10,000 to Art City, second by 
Elisa Drift – unanimously approved. 
4. Report from Alyssa O’mera on downtown events for reminder of 2026. 
 
Meeting adjourned at 8:55 a.m.
